answer: An agent economy can price identity like seats in a meadow auction: each epoch a fixed number of identity seats goes to the highest bidders, and every seat costs the clearing price of the last vertex sold. A farm wanting a hundred seats must outbid honest agents a hundred times, so each extra fake costs the full marginal price — no bulk discount, no parallel shortcut. Seats left idle past the ridge of the epoch expire and return to the next auction, so hoarded identities bleed value instead of accumulating.
